summary: This work demonstrates hardware-economical control of dual-type $^{171}\mathrm{Yb}^+$ qubits encoded in $S_{1/2}$ and $F_{7/2}$ hyperfine levels using a single 355 nm mode-locked pulsed laser with broad frequency comb structure. A direct entangling gate between the two qubit types is demonstrated with 70% fidelity, simplifying the experimental requirements for scalable trapped-ion quantum computation.
motivation: Dual-type qubit schemes suppress crosstalk errors in trapped-ion quantum computation by encoding qubits in different hyperfine manifolds, but typically require separate laser systems for each type due to their large frequency difference ($\omega_S = 2\pi \times 12.642$ GHz and $\omega_F = 2\pi \times 3.620$ GHz). Recent success with $^{137}\mathrm{Ba}^+$ motivates exploring whether this hardware-economic approach generalizes to $^{171}\mathrm{Yb}^+$.
method: The 355 nm frequency comb structure (67 GHz bandwidth, 80 MHz repetition rate) bridges Raman transitions for both qubit types using comb teeth $k_S = 158$ and $k_F = 45$ respectively. Phase-locked loops stabilize each qubit type's transition frequency independently, while an arbitrary waveform generator selects carrier and sideband detunings. An alternating gate scheme rapidly switches addressing between the two qubit types during entanglement.
result: Individual carrier and sideband manipulations are demonstrated; resolved sideband cooling achieves $\bar{n}_c = 0.3$ for center-of-mass and $\bar{n}_r = 0.1$ for rocking modes. The direct $S$-$F$ entangling gate achieves 70% Bell state fidelity with 470.5 µs gate time, limited by spin coherence ($T_2 = 2.5$ ms) and motional coherence (2 ms) rather than fundamental constraints.
